correctness.rationale: Writing the algebra as a one-dimensional extension of an abelian ideal gives the exact bracket [alpha t+u, beta t+v]=alpha A(v)-beta A(u). If alpha is nonzero, the adjoint image is all of im A; if alpha is zero it is zero or the line spanned by A(u). These three exhaustive cases give the rank multiplicities and centralizer sizes. Substitution into the standard adjoint-image formula for d(L) simplifies to (q^r+q^2-1)/q^(r+2). The packaged checker independently reconstructs all adjoint maps for several fields and canonical-form types.

value.rationale: Almost-abelian Lie algebras are a standard all-dimensional solvable family with a complete operator-based structural theory. The theorem gives the full adjoint-rank distribution and exact commutativity-degree spectrum for that family over every finite field, showing that a probability invariant introduced only recently collapses all Jordan-form complexity to the single intrinsic number dim L^2. It also unifies the primary source's two basic rank-one examples and determines exactly what the invariant can recover in this family.
